'''Kaniel Dickens''' (born July 21, 1978) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the second round (50th pick overall) in the [[2000 NBA draft]].

==College career==
Dickens first played [[college basketball]] for Barton Junior College and then [[Tyler Junior College]].  He ended his college career by playing two seasons at the [[University of Idaho]].  At Idaho, Dickens averaged 9.3 points and 5.7 rebounds.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/dickens_feature_070204.html Kaniel Dickens: Learning On The Job – NBA.com] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090103102616/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/dickens_feature_070204.html |date=2009-01-03 }}</ref>

==Professional career==
In addition to being drafted 50th overall by the Jazz, Dickens was drafted 42nd by the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the [[Continental Basketball Association]] and 21st by the [[Las Vegas Silver Bandits]] of the [[International Basketball League (1999–2001)|International Basketball League]].  Dickens played the 2000–01 season for [[PBC Ural Great Perm|Ural Great]] in Russia.<ref name=hoopshype>[http://hoopshype.com/players/kaniel_dickens.htm Kaniel Dickens Profile – Hoopshype.com]</ref>

Dickens was signed as a [[free agent]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] on December 19, 2003, and appeared in 3 games for them during the 2003–04 season. He signed a 10-day contract with the [[New Jersey Nets]] on 01/05/2005 and saw action in 11 games.

===2007–08 season===
Dickens began the 2007–2008 season with the [[Colorado 14ers]] of the [[NBA Development League|NBDL]].  In 29 games (28 starts), prior to his NBA callup, Dickens averaged a team high 20.4 points and 5.2 rebounds.  Dickens was selected to play in the 2008 D-League All-Star Game.

On February 22, 2008, Dickens was signed to a ten-day contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] so they would have enough players to face the Washington Wizards that night, due to a depleted roster because of a blockbuster trade the day prior.<ref>[http://www.ohio.com/news/break_news/15874817.html Cavs sign minor-leaguers]</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3259755 Cavs' last-minute trade for Szczerbiak, Wallace pleases LeBron]</ref>  Dickens saw his first action as a Cavalier on that very night, logging seven minutes with one rebound and a blocked shot.

On March 3, 2008, the Cavaliers signed Dickens to a second ten-day contract.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/dickens_thomas_080303.html Cavaliers Sign Dickens, Thomas To Second 10-Day Contracts]</ref> His contract expired on March 13, 2008, allowing Dickens to become a free agent. Dicken's final NBA game was played on March 6, 2008, in a 96 - 107 loss to the Chicago Bulls. In his final game, Dickens recorded only 2 points and no other stats.

In August 2008 he signed with Italian club [[S.S. Basket Napoli]]. He was waived in September and signed with [[Pallacanestro Varese]] later that month.<ref name=hoopshype/>

In August 2009 he signed a contract with the French [[LNB Pro A|Pro A]] team [[SLUC Nancy]].<ref>[http://sports.orange.fr/cmc/scanner/basket/200932/nancy-wilson-libere-dickens-debarque_239271.html Nancy: Wilson libéré, Dickens débarque]</ref>

For the [[2011 New Zealand NBL season]], Dickens signed with the [[Southland Sharks]].<ref>[http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/4702988/Ex-NBA-player-heads-to-Southland-Sharks Ex NBA player heads to Southland Sharks]</ref>
